# A gate edit locks the conductor out

**Symptom.** Right after a worker edits `claude/hooks/conductor-gate.sh`, every conductor tool call is denied, including `harness` and `cat .harness/...`, with no useful message.

**Cause.** The gate is live: `~/.claude/settings.json` points at the repo file, and it is fail-closed (decision 0005), so a script that exits non-zero denies everything. An unescaped `$(` inside a double-quoted message string was enough (commit 4d9b627 fixed it).

**Fix.** Treat the gate like `bin/`: edit through a new inode (Edit tool or tmp + mv), run `bash -n` and `bash tests/gate.test.sh` before every save, and escape `\$(` and backticks in message strings. If the conductor is already locked out, fix the file from a worker pane; the conductor needs no restart.

rotate_logs "$logf"
  write_progress_md
  return 0
}

# ask_parse_args <agent> <text> [opts...] — the one walk over an ask's options (called by cmd_ask
# after the agent and text checks). Sets ASK_TIMEOUT/FRESH/KEEP.
# The instruction text is positional, so a "--via" inside it is never an option. A bad option,
# --timeout value or --fresh with --keep only sets ASK_BAD: ask_inner turns that into the usage
# error inside the logged subshell (exit 1 is recorded in progress).
ask_parse_args() {
  local agent=$1
  shift 2
  ASK_FRESH=0; ASK_KEEP=0; ASK_BAD=0
  ASK_TIMEOUT=$DEFAULT_TIMEOUT; ASK_TIMEOUT_SET=0
  [ "$agent" != implementer ] || ASK_TIMEOUT=$IMPLEMENTER_TIMEOUT
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --timeout)
        case "${2:-}" in
          ''|*[!0-9]*|0) ASK_BAD=1; shift ;;     # missing/invalid value: usage (logged)
          *) ASK_TIMEOUT=$2; ASK_TIMEOUT_SET=1; shift 2 ;;
        esac ;;
      --fresh) ASK_FRESH=1; shift ;;
      --keep) ASK_KEEP=1; shift ;;
      --via) if [ $# -ge 2 ]; then shift 2; else shift; fi ;;   # no-op until step 5: a running conductor still sends --via skill
      *) ASK_BAD=1; shift ;;
    esac
  done
  [ "$ASK_FRESH$ASK_KEEP" != 11 ] || ASK_BAD=1
}

# rotate_logs <current-log> — newest N logs kept, older than D days deleted; raw headless
# streams are gzipped once a day old and dropped with the logs
rotate_logs() {
  local f
  ls -1t "$LOG_DIR"/*.md 2>/dev/null | grep -vxF -- "$1" | tail -n +"${HARNESS_LOG_KEEP:-200}" \
    | while IFS= read -r f; do rm -f "$f"; done
  find "$LOG_DIR" -name '*.md' -mtime "+${HARNESS_LOG_DAYS:-14}" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -- "$1" | while IFS= read -r f; do rm -f "$f"; done
  find "$LOG_DIR" -name '*.jsonl' -mtime +0 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r f; do gzip -f "$f" 2>/dev/null; done
  find "$LOG_DIR" \( -name '*.jsonl' -o -name '*.jsonl.gz' \) -mtime "+${HARNESS_LOG_DAYS:-14}" 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r f; do rm -f "$f"; done
  return 0
}

# write_progress_md — regenerate .harness/progress.md (<= 60 lines)
check "jsonl: exit" [ "$(jl .exit)" = 0 ]
check "jsonl: status" [ "$(jl .status)" = done ]
check "jsonl: summary" [ "$(jl .summary)" = "analyst report — find things" ]
check "jsonl: instr" [ "$(jl .instr)" = "Describe the repo" ]
check "jsonl: session" [ "$(jl .session)" = "sess-1" ]
check "jsonl: dur_s number" [ "$(jl '.dur_s|type')" = number ]
check "jsonl: ts" jq -e '.ts|test("^[0-9]{4}-")' .harness/progress.jsonl >/dev/null
check "jsonl: verify null for analyst" [ "$(jl '.verify')" = null ]
long=$(printf 'x%.0s' $(seq 1 300))
run ask analyst "$long"
check "jsonl: instr 160 chars" [ "$(jl '.instr|length')" -eq 160 ]
# --via is a no-op until step 5 (a running conductor still sends --via skill): accepted, not sent as text
setup
hook_report analyst '# analyst report — x\nstatus: done\n'
run ask analyst "look" --via skill
check "via no-op: rc 0" [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]
check "via no-op: instr is just the text" [ "$(jl .instr)" = look ]
setup
hook_report analyst '# analyst report — x\nstatus: done\n'
run ask analyst "look" --via
check "via bare: rc 0" [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]
setup
hook_report analyst '# analyst report — x\nstatus: done\n'
run ask analyst "look" --via nope
check "via nope: rc 0" [ "$RC" -eq 0 ]
check "via nope: instr is just the text" [ "$(jl .instr)" = look ]


# --- exit 3 (no report), exit 4 (still running) ----------------------------------------------
setup
FAKE_CLAUDE_MODE=noreport run ask analyst "q"
check "exit3: rc" [ "$RC" -eq 3 ]
check "exit3: jsonl exit" [ "$(jl .exit)" = 3 ]
setup
FAKE_CLAUDE_MODE=slow30 run ask analyst "q" --timeout 1000
check "exit4: rc" [ "$RC" -eq 4 ]
expect allow $C "Glob .harness pattern no path" "$(tool Glob '{"pattern":".harness/reports/*.md"}')"
expect deny  $C "Glob src pattern no path"      "$(tool Glob '{"pattern":"src/**"}')"


# --- Bash: allowlist ---------------------------------------------------------

# ask_parse_args <agent> <text> [opts...] — the one walk over an ask's options (called by cmd_ask
# after the agent and text checks). Sets ASK_TIMEOUT/FRESH/KEEP.
# The instruction text is positional, so a "--via" inside it is never an option. A bad option,
# --timeout value or --fresh with --keep only sets ASK_BAD: ask_inner turns that into the usage
# error inside the logged subshell (exit 1 is recorded in progress).
ask_parse_args() {
  local agent=$1
  shift 2
  ASK_FRESH=0; ASK_KEEP=0; ASK_BAD=0
  ASK_TIMEOUT=$DEFAULT_TIMEOUT; ASK_TIMEOUT_SET=0
  [ "$agent" != implementer ] || ASK_TIMEOUT=$IMPLEMENTER_TIMEOUT
  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
      --timeout)
        case "${2:-}" in
          ''|*[!0-9]*|0) ASK_BAD=1; shift ;;     # missing/invalid value: usage (logged)
          *) ASK_TIMEOUT=$2; ASK_TIMEOUT_SET=1; shift 2 ;;
        esac ;;
      --fresh) ASK_FRESH=1; shift ;;
      --keep) ASK_KEEP=1; shift ;;
      --via) if [ $# -ge 2 ]; then shift 2; else shift; fi ;;   # no-op until step 5: a running conductor still sends --via skill
      *) ASK_BAD=1; shift ;;
    esac
  done

}

   131	# rel PATH -> prints the path relative to CWD, or returns 1 when the path is
   132	# empty, outside CWD, or contains a '..' segment.
   133	rel() {
   134	  local p=$1

   148	# physrel PATH -> prints the symlink-resolved path relative to the resolved CWD
   149	# ("." for CWD itself); returns 1 when it resolves outside CWD, loops, or
   150	# exceeds 16 symlink hops. Needs only cd -P / pwd -P / readlink (bash 3.2, BSD).
   151	# A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing ancestor.
   152	physrel() {
   153	  local p=$1 root full
   154	  root=$(physical "$CWD") || return 1

   156	  full=$(physical "$p") || return 1
   157	  case "$full" in
   158	    "$root") printf '.' ;;
   159	    "$root"/*) printf '%s' "${full#"$root"/}" ;;
   160	    *) return 1 ;;
   161	  esac
   162	}

   164	# physical ABS_PATH -> prints the fully resolved absolute path
   165	physical() {
   166	  local p=$1 hops=0 ex tail par t
   167	  while :; do
   168	    ex=$p; tail=""
   169	    while [ ! -e "$ex" ] && [ ! -L "$ex" ]; do
   170	      [ "$ex" != / ] || return 1
   171	      tail="/${ex##*/}$tail"
   172	      ex=${ex%/*}
   173	      [ -n "$ex" ] || ex=/
   174	    done
   175	    if [ -L "$ex" ]; then
   176	      hops=$((hops + 1))
   177	      [ "$hops" -le 16 ] || return 1
   178	      t=$(readlink "$ex") || return 1
   179	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
   180	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
   181	      case "$t" in /*) p=$t$tail ;; *) p=$par/$t$tail ;; esac
   182	      continue
   183	    fi
   184	    case "$tail" in */..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
   185	    if [ -d "$ex" ]; then
   186	      par=$(cd -P "$ex" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
   187	      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '%s' "$tail"; else printf '%s' "$par$tail"; fi
   188	    else
   189	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
   190	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1

   193	    return 0
   194	  done

   240	
   241	# scan_command -> reads ONE command on stdin, scans it like the shell (single
   242	# quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and prints "<masked><TAB><raw>".
   243	# <masked> is the command with the contents of every '...' / "..." removed
   244	# (quote chars kept); <raw> is the text as written. Exits 1 (= deny) on anything
   245	# that would make it more than one simple command: an unquoted ; & | < > # `
   246	# or newline, an unquoted $( $' $", ` or $( inside double quotes, an
   247	# unterminated quote. Newlines inside quotes are kept as spaces.
   248	# Input must not contain tabs (callers normalize them to spaces).
   249	scan_command() {
   250	  awk '
   251	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; m = ""; r = ""; nl = 0 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double
   252	    {
   253	      line = $0; n = length(line)
   254	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   255	        c = substr(line, i, 1); nx = substr(line, i + 1, 1)
   256	        if (st == 0) {
   257	          if (c == "\\") { c = c substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++; m = m c; r = r c }
   258	          else if (c == ";" || c == "&" || c == "|" || c == "<" || c == ">" || c == "#" || c == "`") bad = 1
   259	          else if (c == "$" && (nx == "(" || nx == "\047" || nx == "\"")) bad = 1
   260	          else {
   261	            m = m c; r = r c
   262	            if (c == "\047") st = 1
   263	            else if (c == "\"") st = 2
   264	          }
   265	        } else if (st == 1) {
   266	          r = r c
   267	          if (c == "\047") { m = m c; st = 0 }
   268	        } else {
   269	          r = r c
   270	          if (c == "\\") { r = r substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++ }
   271	          else if (c == "\"") { m = m c; st = 0 }
   272	          else if (c == "`" || (c == "$" && nx == "(")) bad = 1
   273	        }
   274	      }
   275	      if (st == 0) nl++; else r = r " "
   276	    }
   277	    END { if (st != 0 || bad || nl > 1) exit 1; print m "\t" r }
   278	  '
   279	}

   282	# has_expansion TEXT -> 0 when TEXT contains a character that the shell would

   284	has_expansion() {

   286	    *[\$\{\}\*\?\[\]~\\]*) return 0 ;;

   291	# git_segment_ok RAW -> 0 when a git segment uses no denied option and no

   293	git_segment_ok() {
   294	  local norm
   295	  norm=$(printf ' %s ' "$1" | tr -d "\"'\\\\")

   301	# plain_tok TOKEN -> 0 when TOKEN has no quote or backslash

   305	}

   307	# bodyfile_ok VALUE -> 0 when a gh --body-file / -F value is a path that stays
   308	# (symlinks resolved) under .harness/ or docs/. "-" (stdin) is denied.
   309	bodyfile_ok() {
   310	  local v=$1 p
   311	  [ -n "$v" ] && [ "$v" != - ] || return 1

   315	  p=$(physrel "$v") || return 1

   318	  return 1
   319	}
   320	
   321	# gh_segment_ok MASKED RAW -> 0 only for "gh pr <sub>" with <sub> in GH_ALLOW
   322	# (merge without -d). Global flags -R/--repo/--hostname (and --x=y) may precede
   323	# the group. Everything up to and including the subcommand is read from the
   324	# MASKED segment and must be plain unquoted tokens, so quoting cannot make this
   325	# parser disagree with gh. --body-file/-F values must be plain paths under
   326	# .harness/ or docs/. Flag checks on the rest of the segment use the raw text
   327	# with quoting removed, so "--delete-branch" == --delete-branch.
   328	gh_segment_ok() {
   329	  local norm tok group sub nflag=0 mflag=0 want=0 v
   330	  norm=$(printf '%s ' "$2" | tr -d "\"'\\\\" | tr -s ' ')
   331	  set -f
   332	  set -- $1
   333	  set +f
   334	  shift   # "gh"
   335	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
   336	    plain_tok "$1" || return 1
   337	    case "$1" in
   338	      -R|--repo|--hostname) [ $# -ge 2 ] || return 1; plain_tok "$2" || return 1; shift 2 ;;
   339	      --repo=*|--hostname=*) shift ;;
   340	      -*) return 1 ;;
   341	      *) break ;;
   342	    esac
   343	  done
   344	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
   345	  group=$1
   346	  shift
   347	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
   348	  sub=$1
   349	  shift
   350	  plain_tok "$sub" || return 1
   351	  printf '%s' "$group $sub" | grep -Eq "^($GH_ALLOW)\$" || return 1
   352	  # --body-file / -F values (also --body-file=x, -Fx, clusters like -dF): read
   353	  # from the masked tail, must be plain paths under .harness/ or docs/
   354	  for tok in "$@"; do
   355	    if [ "$want" -eq 1 ]; then want=0; bodyfile_ok "$tok" || return 1; continue; fi
   356	    case "$tok" in
   357	      --body-file|--recover) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); want=1 ;;
   358	      --body-file=*|--recover=*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); bodyfile_ok "${tok#*=}" || return 1 ;;
   359	      --*) ;;
   360	      -*F*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); v=${tok#*F}
   361	            if [ -n "$v" ]; then bodyfile_ok "$v" || return 1; else want=1; fi ;;
   362	    esac
   363	  done
   364	  [ "$want" -eq 0 ] || return 1
   365	  # quote-stripped view: a flag that only appears once quotes are removed
   366	  # ("--body-file") must not slip past the check above, and the per-command
   367	  # flag denials apply to it
   368	  set -f
   369	  set -- $norm
   370	  set +f
   371	  for tok in "$@"; do
   372	    case "$tok" in
   373	      --body-file|--body-file=*|--recover|--recover=*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
   374	      --delete-branch|--delete-branch=*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
   375	      --*) ;;
   376	      -*F*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
   377	    esac
   378	    case "$tok" in
   379	      --*) ;;
   380	      -*d*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
   381	    esac
   382	  done
   383	  [ "$nflag" -le "$mflag" ] || return 1
   384	  return 0
   385	}
   386	
   387	# unquoted_text_ok RAW -> 0 when the segment's shell text is plain. Outside
   388	# quotes only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ % + , : - = and spaces are allowed, and a word
   389	# may not start with = (zsh =cmd) or ~. That rules out braces, globs, glob
   390	# qualifiers, expansions, backslashes, redirects and history bangs in one go.
   391	# Single-quoted text is literal. Double-quoted text may not contain $ ` \ or !.
   392	unquoted_text_ok() {
   393	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | LC_ALL=C awk '
   394	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; ws = 1 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double; ws: still at word start
   395	    { n = length($0)
   396	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   397	        c = substr($0, i, 1)
   398	        if (st == 1) { if (c == "\047") st = 0; else ws = 0 }
   399	        else if (st == 2) {
   400	          if (c == "\"") st = 0
   401	          else {
   402	            ws = 0
   403	            if (c == "$" || c == "`" || c == "\\" || c == "!") bad = 1
   404	          }
   405	        } else if (c == " ") ws = 1
   406	        else if (c == "\047") st = 1            # quotes alone do not end word start
   407	        else if (c == "\"") st = 2
   408	        else if (c == "\\") {                   # only \'"'"', \" and "\ " are literal
   409	          nx = substr($0, i + 1, 1)
   410	          if (nx == "\047" || nx == "\"" || nx == " ") { i++; ws = 0 } else bad = 1
   411	        }
   412	        else if (c ~ /[A-Za-z0-9._\/@%+,:-]/) ws = 0
   413	        else if (c == "=" && !ws) ws = 0
   414	        else bad = 1
   415	      } }
   416	    END { exit (bad || st != 0) ? 1 : 0 }'
   417	}

   419	# cat_ls_segment_ok MASKED -> 0 when a cat / ls segment needs no quoting,
   420	# expansion or parent-directory access
   421	cat_ls_segment_ok() {
   422	  local tok p
   423	  case "$1" in *[\"\']*|*..*) return 1 ;; esac
   424	  has_expansion "$1" && return 1
   425	  set -f
   426	  set -- $1
   427	  set +f
   428	  case "$1" in
   429	    ls)
   430	      shift
   431	      for tok in "$@"; do
   432	        case "$tok" in
   433	          --r*) return 1 ;;            # --recursive (and abbreviations)
   434	          --*) ;;
   435	          -*R*) return 1 ;;            # -R, -laR, ...
   436	          -*) ;;
   437	          *)  p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1   # symlink-resolved path argument
   438	              case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac ;;
   439	        esac
   440	      done ;;
   441	    cat)
   442	      shift
   443	      for tok in "$@"; do        # symlink-resolved: must stay in .harness/ or docs/
   444	        p=$(physrel "$tok") || return 1
   445	        raw_stream_rel "$p" && return 1
   446	        case "$p" in .harness|.harness/*|docs|docs/*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
   447	      done ;;
   448	  esac
   449	  return 0
   450	}
   451	
   452	# bash_ok COMMAND -> 0 when COMMAND is one simple command on the allowlist
   453	bash_ok() {
   454	  local cmd=$1 out seg raw tab
   455	  tab=$(printf '\t')
   456	  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
   457	  cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | tr '\t' ' ')
   458	  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | scan_command) || return 1
   459	  seg=${out%%"$tab"*}
   460	  raw=${out#*"$tab"}
   461	  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   462	  raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   463	  [ -n "$seg" ] || return 1
   464	  # plain shell text only (character allowlist)
   465	  unquoted_text_ok "$raw" || return 1
   466	  # reject '..' path components (but not git ranges like main...HEAD)
   467	  printf ' %s ' "$seg" | grep -Eq '[ /=]\.\.([ /]|$)' && return 1
   468	  case "$seg" in
   469	    git\ *)          git_segment_ok "$raw" || return 1
   470	                     ;;
   471	    gh|gh\ *)        gh_segment_ok "$seg" "$raw" || return 1 ;;
   472	    cat\ *|ls|ls\ *) cat_ls_segment_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
   473	  esac
   474	  printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq "$BASH_ALLOW"
   475	}

   477	case "$TOOL" in

   480	  Read)

   493	      case "$PATTERN" in docs/*|.harness/*) ;; *) deny "$MSG_READ" ;; esac

   495	    else
   496	      readable "$GPATH" || deny "$MSG_READ"
   497	      GBASE=$GPATH

   499	    fi
   500	    # resolve the pattern's static directory prefix (up to the first glob char)
   501	    GPRE=${PATTERN%%[\*\?\[\{]*}
   502	    if [ "$GPRE" = "$PATTERN" ]; then GDIR=$PATTERN
   503	    else case "$GPRE" in */*) GDIR=${GPRE%/*} ;; *) GDIR="" ;; esac

   507	  Bash)
   508	    BCMD=$(field command)
   509	    printf '%s' "$BCMD" | grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*harness[[:space:]]+["'"'"']?watch["'"'"']?([[:space:]]|$)' && deny "$MSG_WATCH"
   510	    bash_ok "$BCMD" || deny "$MSG_BASH" ;;

   131	# rel PATH -> prints the path relative to CWD, or returns 1 when the path is
   132	# empty, outside CWD, or contains a '..' segment.
   133	rel() {
   134	  local p=$1
   135	  [ -n "$p" ] || return 1
   136	  case "$p" in
   137	    ..|../*|*/..|*/../*|'~'*) return 1 ;;
   138	  esac
   139	  case "$p" in
   140	    "$CWD")   p="." ;;
   141	    "$CWD"/*) p=${p#"$CWD"/} ;;
   142	    /*)       return 1 ;;
   143	    ./*)      p=${p#./} ;;
   144	  esac
   145	  printf '%s' "$p"
   146	}

   148	# physrel PATH -> prints the symlink-resolved path relative to the resolved CWD
   149	# ("." for CWD itself); returns 1 when it resolves outside CWD, loops, or
   150	# exceeds 16 symlink hops. Needs only cd -P / pwd -P / readlink (bash 3.2, BSD).
   151	# A path that does not exist yet resolves through its nearest existing ancestor.
   152	physrel() {
   153	  local p=$1 root full
   154	  root=$(physical "$CWD") || return 1
   155	  case "$p" in /*) ;; *) p=$CWD/$p ;; esac
   156	  full=$(physical "$p") || return 1
   157	  case "$full" in
   158	    "$root") printf '.' ;;
   159	    "$root"/*) printf '%s' "${full#"$root"/}" ;;
   160	    *) return 1 ;;
   161	  esac
   162	}
   163	
   164	# physical ABS_PATH -> prints the fully resolved absolute path
   165	physical() {
   166	  local p=$1 hops=0 ex tail par t
   167	  while :; do
   168	    ex=$p; tail=""
   169	    while [ ! -e "$ex" ] && [ ! -L "$ex" ]; do
   170	      [ "$ex" != / ] || return 1
   171	      tail="/${ex##*/}$tail"
   172	      ex=${ex%/*}
   173	      [ -n "$ex" ] || ex=/
   174	    done
   175	    if [ -L "$ex" ]; then
   176	      hops=$((hops + 1))
   177	      [ "$hops" -le 16 ] || return 1
   178	      t=$(readlink "$ex") || return 1
   179	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
   180	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
   181	      case "$t" in /*) p=$t$tail ;; *) p=$par/$t$tail ;; esac
   182	      continue
   183	    fi
   184	    case "$tail" in */..|*/../*) return 1 ;; esac
   185	    if [ -d "$ex" ]; then
   186	      par=$(cd -P "$ex" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
   187	      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '%s' "$tail"; else printf '%s' "$par$tail"; fi
   188	    else
   189	      par=${ex%/*}; [ -n "$par" ] || par=/
   190	      par=$(cd -P "$par" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || return 1
   191	      if [ "$par" = / ]; then printf '/%s%s' "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; else printf '%s/%s%s' "$par" "${ex##*/}" "$tail"; fi
   192	    fi
   193	    return 0
   194	  done
   195	}

   241	# scan_command -> reads ONE command on stdin, scans it like the shell (single
   242	# quotes, double quotes, backslash escapes) and prints "<masked><TAB><raw>".
   243	# <masked> is the command with the contents of every '...' / "..." removed
   244	# (quote chars kept); <raw> is the text as written. Exits 1 (= deny) on anything
   245	# that would make it more than one simple command: an unquoted ; & | < > # `
   246	# or newline, an unquoted $( $' $", ` or $( inside double quotes, an
   247	# unterminated quote. Newlines inside quotes are kept as spaces.
   248	# Input must not contain tabs (callers normalize them to spaces).
   249	scan_command() {
   250	  awk '
   251	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; m = ""; r = ""; nl = 0 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double
   252	    {
   253	      line = $0; n = length(line)
   254	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   255	        c = substr(line, i, 1); nx = substr(line, i + 1, 1)
   256	        if (st == 0) {
   257	          if (c == "\\") { c = c substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++; m = m c; r = r c }
   258	          else if (c == ";" || c == "&" || c == "|" || c == "<" || c == ">" || c == "#" || c == "`") bad = 1
   259	          else if (c == "$" && (nx == "(" || nx == "\047" || nx == "\"")) bad = 1
   260	          else {
   261	            m = m c; r = r c
   262	            if (c == "\047") st = 1
   263	            else if (c == "\"") st = 2
   264	          }
   265	        } else if (st == 1) {
   266	          r = r c
   267	          if (c == "\047") { m = m c; st = 0 }
   268	        } else {
   269	          r = r c
   270	          if (c == "\\") { r = r substr(line, i + 1, 1); i++ }
   271	          else if (c == "\"") { m = m c; st = 0 }
   272	          else if (c == "`" || (c == "$" && nx == "(")) bad = 1
   273	        }
   274	      }
   275	      if (st == 0) nl++; else r = r " "
   276	    }
   277	    END { if (st != 0 || bad || nl > 1) exit 1; print m "\t" r }
   278	  '
   279	}

   321	# gh_segment_ok MASKED RAW -> 0 only for "gh pr <sub>" with <sub> in GH_ALLOW
   322	# (merge without -d). Global flags -R/--repo/--hostname (and --x=y) may precede
   323	# the group. Everything up to and including the subcommand is read from the
   324	# MASKED segment and must be plain unquoted tokens, so quoting cannot make this
   325	# parser disagree with gh. --body-file/-F values must be plain paths under
   326	# .harness/ or docs/. Flag checks on the rest of the segment use the raw text
   327	# with quoting removed, so "--delete-branch" == --delete-branch.
   328	gh_segment_ok() {
   329	  local norm tok group sub nflag=0 mflag=0 want=0 v
   330	  norm=$(printf '%s ' "$2" | tr -d "\"'\\\\" | tr -s ' ')
   331	  set -f
   332	  set -- $1
   333	  set +f
   334	  shift   # "gh"
   335	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
   336	    plain_tok "$1" || return 1
   337	    case "$1" in
   338	      -R|--repo|--hostname) [ $# -ge 2 ] || return 1; plain_tok "$2" || return 1; shift 2 ;;
   339	      --repo=*|--hostname=*) shift ;;
   340	      -*) return 1 ;;
   341	      *) break ;;
   342	    esac
   343	  done
   344	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
   345	  group=$1
   346	  shift
   347	  [ $# -ge 1 ] || return 1
   348	  sub=$1
   349	  shift
   350	  plain_tok "$sub" || return 1
   351	  printf '%s' "$group $sub" | grep -Eq "^($GH_ALLOW)\$" || return 1
   352	  # --body-file / -F values (also --body-file=x, -Fx, clusters like -dF): read
   353	  # from the masked tail, must be plain paths under .harness/ or docs/
   354	  for tok in "$@"; do
   355	    if [ "$want" -eq 1 ]; then want=0; bodyfile_ok "$tok" || return 1; continue; fi
   356	    case "$tok" in
   357	      --body-file|--recover) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); want=1 ;;
   358	      --body-file=*|--recover=*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); bodyfile_ok "${tok#*=}" || return 1 ;;
   359	      --*) ;;
   360	      -*F*) mflag=$((mflag + 1)); v=${tok#*F}
   361	            if [ -n "$v" ]; then bodyfile_ok "$v" || return 1; else want=1; fi ;;
   362	    esac
   363	  done
   364	  [ "$want" -eq 0 ] || return 1
   365	  # quote-stripped view: a flag that only appears once quotes are removed
   366	  # ("--body-file") must not slip past the check above, and the per-command
   367	  # flag denials apply to it
   368	  set -f
   369	  set -- $norm
   370	  set +f
   371	  for tok in "$@"; do
   372	    case "$tok" in
   373	      --body-file|--body-file=*|--recover|--recover=*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
   374	      --delete-branch|--delete-branch=*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
   375	      --*) ;;
   376	      -*F*) nflag=$((nflag + 1)) ;;
   377	    esac
   378	    case "$tok" in
   379	      --*) ;;
   380	      -*d*) [ "$group $sub" != 'pr merge' ] || return 1 ;;
   381	    esac
   382	  done
   383	  [ "$nflag" -le "$mflag" ] || return 1
   384	  return 0
   385	}

   387	# unquoted_text_ok RAW -> 0 when the segment's shell text is plain. Outside
   388	# quotes only A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ % + , : - = and spaces are allowed, and a word
   389	# may not start with = (zsh =cmd) or ~. That rules out braces, globs, glob
   390	# qualifiers, expansions, backslashes, redirects and history bangs in one go.
   391	# Single-quoted text is literal. Double-quoted text may not contain $ ` \ or !.
   392	unquoted_text_ok() {
   393	  printf '%s\n' "$1" | LC_ALL=C awk '
   394	    BEGIN { st = 0; bad = 0; ws = 1 }   # st: 0 unquoted, 1 single, 2 double; ws: still at word start
   395	    { n = length($0)
   396	      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   397	        c = substr($0, i, 1)
   398	        if (st == 1) { if (c == "\047") st = 0; else ws = 0 }
   399	        else if (st == 2) {
   400	          if (c == "\"") st = 0
   401	          else {
   402	            ws = 0
   403	            if (c == "$" || c == "`" || c == "\\" || c == "!") bad = 1
   404	          }
   405	        } else if (c == " ") ws = 1
   406	        else if (c == "\047") st = 1            # quotes alone do not end word start
   407	        else if (c == "\"") st = 2
   408	        else if (c == "\\") {                   # only \'"'"', \" and "\ " are literal
   409	          nx = substr($0, i + 1, 1)
   410	          if (nx == "\047" || nx == "\"" || nx == " ") { i++; ws = 0 } else bad = 1
   411	        }
   412	        else if (c ~ /[A-Za-z0-9._\/@%+,:-]/) ws = 0
   413	        else if (c == "=" && !ws) ws = 0
   414	        else bad = 1
   415	      } }
   416	    END { exit (bad || st != 0) ? 1 : 0 }'
   417	}

   452	# bash_ok COMMAND -> 0 when COMMAND is one simple command on the allowlist
   453	bash_ok() {
   454	  local cmd=$1 out seg raw tab
   455	  tab=$(printf '\t')
   456	  [ -n "$cmd" ] || return 1
   457	  cmd=$(printf '%s' "$cmd" | tr '\t' ' ')
   458	  out=$(printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | scan_command) || return 1
   459	  seg=${out%%"$tab"*}
   460	  raw=${out#*"$tab"}
   461	  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   462	  raw=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   463	  [ -n "$seg" ] || return 1
   464	  # plain shell text only (character allowlist)
   465	  unquoted_text_ok "$raw" || return 1
   466	  # reject '..' path components (but not git ranges like main...HEAD)
   467	  printf ' %s ' "$seg" | grep -Eq '[ /=]\.\.([ /]|$)' && return 1
   468	  case "$seg" in
   469	    git\ *)          git_segment_ok "$raw" || return 1
   470	                     ;;
   471	    gh|gh\ *)        gh_segment_ok "$seg" "$raw" || return 1 ;;
   472	    cat\ *|ls|ls\ *) cat_ls_segment_ok "$seg" || return 1 ;;
   473	  esac
   474	  printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq "$BASH_ALLOW"
   475	}
